Ban the sale of wood burners in the UK, Air pollution in the UK is linked to 40,000 deaths.

Indoor air pollution has increased, though domestic combustion.

Banning the sale of wood burners protects the health and safety of citizens and neighbourhoods., Small particles (PM2.5) coming from wood burners enter the human body  and are a health hazard. 

There has already been regulation against the sale of 'wet wood' and coal. 

New regulations are due in Jan 2022 for 'Eco designs' that still emit dangerous amounts of pollution. 

Let's go one further. 

Let's ban the sale of these household hazards.

Make parking on pavements a criminal offence, and fund preventative measures, The Government should make parking on pavements a criminal offence, and also provide funding to local authorities to install physical barriers between roads and pavements to make this impossible., Too many motorists inconsiderately park on pavements, causing obstructions to pedestrians and people that use wheelchairs or mobility scooters.

The British Public want to SACK Boris Johnson, Boris Johnson can no longer be trusted to obey the rules he created for the United Kingdom and should be SACKED for the continuous lying in the House of Commons., Remove Boris Johnson from Government. He has lost the trust of the people. He is not to be trusted with the amount of scandals that surround him.

Make the Ministerial code legally binding to ensure accountability and ethics., By making the Ministerial code and seven principles of public life legally binding will  ensure sound professional conduct confidence in our leaders., In light of the recent media reported breaches of the Ministerial code and seven principles of public life the British public are seeing repeated unethical and unprofessional behaviour. Accountability must be underpinned by the law as it is in other professions.
It is not fair to have code of conduct laws for other professions. This disparity is eroding trust and respect.
Ltns Oxfordshire, reconsider the LTns in oxford as we all feel trapped and the council dose not listen to us and people are dieing because of it help us,

Stop private parking  organisations and companies stealing from the public, Put a stop to busineses that are private car parking enforcement and to stop the theft of public peoples monies and the unfair harassment to people and citizens, Stop private parking businesses from issuing unfair parking fines and stop them stealing fro. The public

To Recall the MP of Lichfield district and call for a bi election, Recall of MPs Act 2015 (c. 25), To Forse Lichfield mp to vacate there seat in Parliament and call for a bi election.
Due to ignoring there duties to their constituents

Any elected MP who switches party MUST face a bi-election!, When an elected official is elected to a seat they are put there by the voters voting for the party of their choice, when that elected official then switches to another political party they are in effect switching voters from a party they voted for to a party they did not.

This is unacceptable, Make it mandatory that any elected official MUST surrender their seat until they are elected to it for the party they switch to.

Make private parking penalties unenforceable through the court system., To stop private parking companies being able to enforce unreasonable charges and fines through the courts, the Government should make private parking penalties unenforceable. The Government stopped clamping on private property, but a CCJ can be worse as they affect credit history., The Government needs to protect motorists from legal enforcement of private parking charges. It can affect people’s livelihoods and mental health. What gives operators of private parking the right to affect the credit rating of a person for the next 5 years? Many use scare tactics to charge excessive sums. The Government stopped wheel clamping in private car parks and now they need to stop this.

A By-election to be called for any place that the MP defects from a party., To hold a by election in any ward where a sitting MP choses to leave the party he/she was elected in. This to be Made Law., Make it a law that any sitting/elected MP moving parties, crossing the floor a by election in that ward is held. This is to be fair to the electorate as they might have voted or a party rather than a person, which is normally the case, And not to have another party's political views thrust upon that electorate.

Back Boris Johnson as UK Prime Minister, There is a vicious media campaign against our democratically elected PM which is gathering speed and momentum., We see horrific media broadcasts where UK Government ministers are being questioned like primary school children and the whole government is being held in huge disrespect at this very important time.

World affairs mean that our Government needs the support of the UK media as well as the country as a whole.  We ask Parliament to back Boris for the good of our nation!

Stop the Leicester City Council workpkace parking levy, To stop the plan by Leicester council to introduce a parking levy of £550 per parking place per year. Either employers will have to pay or pass this onto employees. This includes schools losing money that sit in the proposed boundary., The proposal to fund for greener transport puts essentially an unfair tax on people who choose to work or have a business in Leicester. Many people work in Leicester but travel from further afield and are paying money for a system they will not benefit. Salaries will not increase to reflect this. Essential services will lose money to the council eg schools and other education settings. Money that cannot be spared

Covid travel tests should be axed for unvaccinated too., We want the government to stop discriminating against individuals who have chosen not to be vaccinated. Being vaccinated is a choice which the individual can make under the Humans right Act 1998, we should not be restricted in traveling or work as both vaccinated and unvaccinated can carry the virus, We want the government to abolish the rules against unvaccinated individuals who chose to travel as we believe this against our free will and we shouldn’t be treated like enemies within our own country. We also want the government to abolish the rules on NHS staff having to be fully vaccinated as again this is a personal choice and any attempt to force the vaccine would be a violation of our bodily autonomy and would breach human rights law and international treaties on medical treatment.

Stop ministers from using a private jet for Government business , Government ministers should not use a private jet to conduct Government business. They should use everyday flights. , In these times when people are struggling to meet ends meet, this is a perk ministers can do without.

Require schools ringfence funding for pupils with Education and Healthcare Plans, The Government should require that schools ringfence funding required to deliver Education and Healthcare Plan (EHCPs). Currently schools have discretion about funding allocations, even though there are obligations to deliver EHCPs. This can mean pupils with EHCP don't receive the support they need., The Government should ensure that budgets for the education of each pupil with SEN who has an EHCP are spent on support for that child.
 
When children with SEN don't have their special educational needs met they can end up excluded, traumatised, even ill-treated due to behaviours arising from them not coping. This can have consequences across their lives, and affect their whole families.
Force No10 to publish Sue Gray’s report available in full to the general public., For MPs told hold a debate in Parliament in the full report from Sue Gray., To uphold democracy in British government

Revoke rules against accusing MPs of deliberate falsehoods in House of Commons, The existing rules that prevent the accusing of MPs of ‘deliberate falsehoods’ in the House of Commons should be revoked., The Ministerial code states “holders of public office should be truthful” and “It is of paramount importance that ministers give accurate and truthful information to parliament, correcting any inadvertent error at the earliest opportunity." Changing the rules would therefore support compliance with the Code, ensuring that any wrong information given by MPs is swiftly corrected. Those MPs that make accusations of dishonesty are sanctioned by the existing rules, which is wrong.

Do not reform the Human Rights Act, The proposed Human Rights Act reforms must be withdrawn. The Government must not make any changes to the Human Rights Act, especially ones that dilute people's human rights in any circumstances, make the Government less accountable, or reduce people's ability to make human rights claims., The Human Rights Act as it exists currently protects all of us. We lose it at our peril. It is an essential law that allows us to challenge public authorities when they get it wrong and has helped secure justice on issues from the right to life to the right to free speech.
 
The Human Rights Act has changed many lives for the better. It must be protected, and not subject to reforms that reduce its scope and limit when people can rely on it.

Abolish the Human Rights Act Reform proposals, The proposed changes to the Human Rights Act risk stripping individuals of their basic human rights and freedoms., The changes to this Act drastically reduce protection from government draconian measures. These reforms cannot become statute.

Unless the reforms to the Human Rights Act are thrown out, we will lose freedoms on an unprecedented scale. This proposed legislation should galvanise opposition on all sides of the political spectrum. This grotesque authoritarianism must be stopped.

Ban gambling adverts on TV, Radio and social media before 9pm, Gambling advertising is everywhere, often endorsed by celebrities, and with catchy theme tunes. These adverts glamourise and normalise gambling to the young and vulnerable., Gambling is restricted to adults, and should not be advertised before the 9pm watershed.
 
I myself suffered a gambling addiction. This cost me more than money. I lost friends, self-esteem, self-worth, confidence. I even suffered with mental health issues.
 
Too many people suffer gambling addiction, which can lead to tragic consequences.
 
Gambling should not be allowed to be advertised on TV, radio or social media before 9pm.

Require all Home Office allowed appeals to be implemented within 8 weeks, The Government should ensure that all allowed appeals are implemented within 8 weeks, which used to be the Home Office target., Many families are depressed and devastated due to delays in implementing allowed appeals. Reports suggest that some have gone over 6 months to one year.

Create a new residents permit band for electric motorcycles and mopeds in London, The cost of a residents permit for a fully electric car is £25 per year, for any motorbike it is £60 and there is no option for electric motorbikes. The council are not prepared to change this ‘at this time’. 
https://www.islington.gov.uk/parking/parking-permits/resident-permit-costs-checker, I’m requesting that all London councils review their motorbike parking charged and set a reasonable tariff for parking a fully electric motorbike or moped, relative to the electric car charge.

Electric motorbikes are becoming more common and should be accommodated for like all other electric vehicles, they reduce pollution and congestion on our roads and it shouldn’t be prohibitively expensive to park one outside your home.

Hold a UK Public Referendum on the Reforms of the Human Rights Act (HRA) 1998., The Lord Chancellor has published a consultation to reform the HRA 1998 and replace it, with a Bill of Rights (BoR).

Parliament must intervene and draft legislation to hold a Referendum and let the  the people of the UK decide, whether to retain the HRA, or allow it to repealed by a BoR., The will and consent of the people is hath required to permit the Lord Chancellor to repeal our HRA with a BoR.

Therefore, these consultation reforms must be halted, and a referendum held for all the people to decide on the future of our HRA.

Trigger Article 16, Trigger Article 16 of the Northern Ireland protocol. We shouldn't have an invisible border within our own country., The situation in Northern Ireland cannot be allowed to continue. What's happened in Northern Ireland recently shows that there is only one solution to the problem. A solution that should've been implemented last July, but the British government was, and still is, too cowardly to do it. Which is why the EU are basically laughing at us. The government must stop being all mouth and no trousers, trigger Article 16 and then not back out until the EU are on their knees begging.

vote of no confidence in the standing government on behalf of the UK public, Government officials have stated the real public do not care about lockdown parties. It is public record that parties took place while the public were restricted in movement, socialisation and even in their grieving for loved ones., I want Parliament to see the public do care about lockdown parties and the behaviours of the standing government. I want it acknowledged that we the uk public have lost confidence in our countries leaders and no longer want them to represent us on a national or international level.

Require all police conduct complaints & appeals to be referred to the IOPC, The Government should amend the Police Reform Act 2002 to remove individual police forces’ right to investigate complaints and appeals against its own officers’ conduct. Such complaints and appeals should always be referred to the Independent Office for Police Conduct (IOPC)., This would help to ensure that there is no perception of bias in how such complaints and appeals are handled.

Change petition rules to allow petitions of no confidence in the UK Government, Petitions asking for a vote of no confidence in an individual Minister or the Government as a whole are against petition rules. This means UK citizens are at the whim of MPs to challenge standing government as we are unable to do so ourselves. 

Anger at #Partygate is at an all time high., I want petitioning rules changed to allow UK citizens the ability to show no confidence in the standing government and/or Prime Minister. 

This is my 4th attempt to petition challenge against the Government following #Partygate and it should not be so difficult to make myself heard.

Stop falsehoods and slurs being made and repeated in the House of Commons., The leaders of our country should be an example to us and display exemplary behaviour. Where their behaviour is unlawful that is a matter for the police, when poor behaviour like falsehoods or slurs takes place in the House of Commons the Speaker should fulfil his/her role and address it., The Speaker’s role is to keep order in The House, & to maintain and upkeep Parliamentary Standards. If he permits the continued repetition of falsehoods without taking action to correct the record, or fails to fulfil the role of his job & bring members into line who then continue to repeat falsehoods, he allows lying to become the norm, thereby betraying the electorate who are rendered unable to make informed decisions at election time. Ask the Speaker to fulfil his remit & stop this occurring.

Hold a confidence/no confidence referendum on the government every 2.5 years , Mid-way through a Prime Minister’s time in office (5 years), a referendum should be held on whether the general public has confidence, or no confidence, in the current government. If a majority vote 'no confidence' this should then lead to a general election., It is seen that only Parliament has the power to dissolve the government, why should the general public not get a more regular say in whether the government and Prime Minister are doing an acceptable job? Not only that, even if a high proportion of Parliament does not have confidence in the government, due to the need for a two-third majority, it is very hard to trigger an early general election. Why should the public not have a more regular say in whether they believe the government is representing them?

Ban fur and foie gras imports, It has been widely reported that the UK Government is considering dropping plans to ban imports of fur and foie gras. We want the Government to confirm that the Animal Abroad Bill will include provisions to ban the import of fur and foie gras to the UK., The production of fur and foie gras causes suffering and by allowing the products to be imported the UK is enabling that cruelty.

Ministers should be focused on other issues facing the country rather than considering dropping the proposed ban and continuing to allow cruelly made items into the country.

Personal choice over what we buy is one thing but enabling animal cruelty is quite another. The ban should be implemented and our stance against animal cruelty made firm.

Hold a referendum on any changes to or repeal of the Human Rights Act, I want a National Referendum to be held to ask the public for approval of any changes to, or repeal of, the Human Rights Act. This is for the people to decide. Not the State., The Human Rights Act as it exists currently protects all of us. We lose it at our peril. It is an essential law that allows us to challenge public authorities when they get it wrong and has helped secure justice on issues from the right to life to the right to free speech.

Order an official probe into potential Russian interference in the EU referendum, The formal demand from the Parliament's Intelligence and Security Committee to 'write a full assessment of potential Russian interference in the EU referendum and publish an unclassified summary' must be done., It has been 2 years since the Russia Report was released and The ISC said the UK Intelligence Community should now write an assessment of "potential Russian interference in the EU referendum" and publish an "unclassified summary", "to establish whether a hostile state took deliberate action with with the aim of influencing a UK democratic process." This must be done to uphold our democracy. It has not been done. The public deserve to know how much this referendum may have been influenced by Russia.
More support for parents with special educational needs children, Help fund and establish further support,

Remove the newly implemented 20mph speed limit in Buckley, Flintshire., The newly implemented 20mph speed limit should only be in housing estates and around schools during school start/end time., It is causing frustrated drivers, leading to increased road rage and a higher chance of collision. 20mpg is also too slow to overtake a cyclist or slow moving vehicle such as a tractor with out breaking the speed limit. 

There has already been a collision on the day that the new speed limit was introduced. There is also not enough signs to effevtively inform drivers of the new speed limit

Stop people buying property in the lake district national park for holiday lets, Stop people buying property in the lake district national park n turning them into holiday let's and also stop estate agents advertising propery to be turned into holiday let's, There not enough afordable housing in the lake district for people to buy but the rich come from London n torn them into holiday let's then no one can buy property

Hold a referendum on the government's proposed reforms to the Human Rights Act, The proposed reforms to the Human Rights Act represent a major shift of power from people and courts to the government, effectively placing parliament above the law and unable to be challenged. Such proposals should be discussed and scrutinised nationally, If these proposals are implemented then the government would have supreme unassailable power to do whatever it wants without challenge, the courts and people would be powerless. This country would no longer be a democracy. The ability of courts to challenge 'bad' law would be removed and individual basic rights only upheld if the government decides it is in the 'public good' to do so. This vague condition could, and probably would, lead to massive abuse. Open and national debate must take place.

Against pay permile and speed limiters as they are a infringement of rights, Charger EVs by sizes on yearly road tax 
Say £75 for small ones
£150 for mid size 
And £200 for mpvs and 4x4 EVs, Get rid off the pay permile tarkers and speed limiters as they are dangerous also is a from of spying on us and a infringement of our human rights

Require schools close at 1pm on Friday so Muslims can go to mosque, It's important to many Christians to go to church on Sunday, Jews to go to synagogue on Saturday, and Muslims to go to mosque on Friday. However, most schools don't finish on Friday until after prayer is over. We want schools to close at 1pm on Fridays, so Muslim students can go to pray at mosque., I want the Government to require all schools to close by 1pm on Friday to help Muslim students practise their faith.

Have a system in place where one can view outstanding parking fines and pay them, Have a system in place or help us put a system in place where one can access all their parking fines in one place and pay them. It is not always clear which parking fines are outstanding. An example being; if you change your address there is a backlog in the system for parking alerts to be sent., Create a system or put a universal parking system in place that connects to all the parking companies/councils available so that individuals can view their outstanding fines and pay them. The debt collectors can 'trace' where individuals are and send them the debt collection notice. Individual's credit score being affected, less people able to use credit and the issue escalates because of a poorly managed system. Individuals should be informed of all outstanding fines outside of post and online.

Set stricter legal targets for air quality and increase funding for research, The Government’s planned new legal targets for air quality must align with the WHO air quality guideline levels. It should also increase funding for research and development to develop cleaner energy sources and reduce plastic air pollution from tyres. This will also help combat climate change., Each year at least 28,000 people in the UK die prematurely because of air pollution, including children. Air pollution has been linked to heart disease, lung disease and cancer, and can exacerbate allergies, skin conditions and pregnancy complications. 
 
Currently we are above the World Health Organisation guideline levels for multiple pollutants. Data from the World Bank shows that 66% of the UK population were exposed to pollution above the WHO standards in 2017.
Give back the Parthenon Marbles to Greece, To set a date in 2022 to deliver the marbles back to Greece, To right a wrong and give the Marbles back to where they belong

Free parking for NHS staff, Having had to work during the pandemic in unprecedented  pressures please for the loyalty to all the NHS staff make parking free In all hospitals for staff, Because of the cost of living going up and tax rises and energy bills please give all the NHS staff at least one less thing to worry about by having to make extra money by doing extra long hours to pay for parking at there workplace

Implement online voting for general elections and referendums in the UK, We would like for people to be able to vote online as well as in person for general elections and referendums in the UK. Procedures would need to be put in place to ensure everyone is only able to vote once, either in person or online., We believe that implementing online voting could help reduce the cost of elections, and increase voter turnout by making it easier to vote, especially for those with disabilities that make voting in person challenging, and for young people, who were the least likely age group to vote in the last general election.

Reform arrangements for practical driving tests to tackle backlog, Give registered driving instructors the role of 'signing off' learner drivers as competent at driving manoeuvres, and only allow a practical test to be booked once a learner is signed off in this way. The reversing exercise could then be removed from the practical test., These changes would mean that the practical driving test would be shorter, as there would be no need to test learners on a reversing manoeuvre, and by allowing a practical driving test to be booked once a learner is signed off by a registered driving instructor, it will stop tests being booked by people who simply want to 'have a go'. This should help increase availability of driving tests, and reduce the backlog.

Impose new restrictions on the placement mobile speed cameras, We want the Government to restrict the placement of mobile speed cameras so they can only be located in places that are legally parking spaces, and on flat stretches of road., We believe it is unfair that mobile speed cameras can be situated on verges or other areas where cars cannot legally parked, and on ascents or descents, that can impact the speed of a vehicle.

The Prime Minister and Chancellor have lied to parliament and must resign, This shouldn’t be optional. It should be automatic. If ministers refuse to resign after misleading parliament they should be sacked by the Speaker, Because Democracy must be protected from liars

Conservative MPs to hold their leader to account and remove Johnson from office, Conservative MPs are rallying around their leader, even in the face of his lawbreaking, acting out of a concern for their own ideals, interests, or sense of loyalty. They must act in the national interest, submit letters of no-confidence to the 1922 Committee, or allow a censure motion to pass., By breaking mandatory quarantine rules, Boris Johnson has committed a criminal offence.

By maintaining Johnson in office despite his lawbreaking, Conservative backbenchers will have destroyed the principle of integrity upon which the survival of the Ministerial Code depends. The subsequent constitutional crisis will overwhelm the Union and the unwritten constitution itself.

Boris Johnson and Rishi Sunak - hold them accountable for breaking the law, The positions of responsibility these two law breaking Ministers hold completely undermines any integrity of the British parliamentary system. I call for their immediate suspension, and that their suitability to hold positions of responsibility and power be reviewed as a matter of urgency., It is completely incomprehensible that ministers, who have complete disregard for laws that they themselves made, and demanded the British public adhere to, should remain in office in British parliament. They should be held to the highest accountability standards and scrutiny. 
It completely undermines the confidence of the British public for these senior ministers to remain in office. I believe I speak for the majority of the British populace. End corruption at the head of government!

Rishi Sunak and Boris Johnson must resign, After breaking roles, made by themselves country leaders Boris Johnson and Rishi Sunak must resign, Because this is a terrible example for the entire society and I believe that anyone who breaks the law should be allowed to remain Prime Minister or Chancellor.

Introduce independent body to enforce the ministerial code on ministers., It is clear that our democracy is broken and there is no accountability to the people in the highest form of Government. There needs to be a body which has the power to enforce the ministerial code on Ministers., If Ministers create laws that they then break then they no longer retain the faith of many of the people. The current lack of accountability is shocking. People who make the law should set an example. Breaking the law, especially one you made should automatically mean being removed as a minister and barred from high office. Their needs to be an independent body with the power to remove ministers when they flout the ministerial code.

Boris Johnson and Rishi Sunak broke the law. They must resign. End of story., PM Boris Johnson must resign as Prime Minister and Rishi Sunak must resign as Chancellor after being caught breaking the coronavirus lockdown. They attended parties in Westminster which broke their own lockdown rules. They partied while people died. They must go., In April 2020 Catherine Calderwood, Scotland’s Chief Medical Officer, resigned after breaking the coronavirus lockdown.
In May 2020 Professor Neil Ferguson, the epidemiologist who shaped the government's coronavirus strategy, resigned after breaking the lockdown rules.
In December 2021 Allegra Stratton resigned as government spokesperson on being caught mocking "partygate".
April 2022 Boris Johnson will not resign as PM after being caught repeatedly breaking the coronavirus lockdown. Why Not?

An MP found guilty of breaking any law is automatically subject to recall., Current legislation means that MPs who break the law can be subject to recall by their constituents. However it is only in narrowly defined circumstances. Parliament can amend the legislation to ensure that all MPs who break the law must answer to their constituents., Recent high profile cases of MPs found guilty of breaking the law have trashed the reputation of the country. This change would go some way to restoring that reputation. It would also put responsibility for representation where it belongs - to the electorate that voted the MP in the first place.

Sack the Prime minister and Chancellor, We the people need to be led by law abiding citizens, by refusing to abide by the minstrel code and not resign they are making a mockery of the whole system. You lead by example so do the honourable thing and resign!, Use the minstrel code to have them removed from office!

Law makers should not be law breakers. Change the ministerial code., Debate the changing of the ministerial code to:
A) Be independent of government, removing the the PM as ultimate arbitrator.
B) Increase the consequences for those found to be in breach of the code.
C) Require cabinet ministers who are found guilty of law breaking to resign their position., Government ministers have been shown to not only break the rules of the ministerial code but in some cases to have also broken the law (even laws that they themselves have made). The current ability of the prime minister to be the ultimate arbitrator of ministerial code has been shown to be flawed whilst the PM is as guilty as those for which he arbitrator. This cannot be acceptable and needs to change.

Hold a referendum on using the Additional Member System for General Elections, I would like the Government to hold a referendum, to give the British public the Chance to change the way we vote in UK general elections. The question should be whether we adopt an Additional Member System (AMS) such as the one used in Scottish and Welsh parliamentary elections., I believe the UK's current electoral system is very unfair, and favours some political parties while completely under-representing others. The Additional Member System is already used in Scotland and Wales. In Scotland in particular, it has produced more representative election results as opposed to the current First Past the Post electoral system used for General Elections.

Require Ministers found to break the law be removed from office and lose pension, Any Ministers of Government, including the Prime Minister found to be guilty of breaking any laws should be removed from ministerial office and Parliament, and stripped of any pension rights they accrued from ministerial office.,
Make it legal to smoke in pubs after 9pm, Allow smoking in pubs after 9pm,

End mandatory coalition in the Northern Ireland Executive, It is time to overhaul how the executive is formed in Northern Ireland. Mandatory coalition does not work. We have moved on from 1998 and it is time to end rules that distribute ministerial posts to multiple parties representing different communities. It is time for change., Currently ministers are nominated by the political parties in the Northern Ireland Assembly, on the basis of their share of seats in the Assembly. Additionally, the First and deputy First Ministers must be from parties representing different parts of the community.
 
This has led to stalemates, and the absence of a functioning executive and assembly.
 
The Government must reform these rules so Northern Ireland can be governed by any party or coalition that can command the confidence of the Assembly.
 
The current format of government hasn't worked for at least the last 10 years and forcing parties who are world apart in ideology to "work" together has failed, the people of Northern Ireland deserve better.

Electrical installation work only completed by registered electrician, Hold the NICEIC or similar bodies Accountable to take more action in being responsible for all electrical installation work being installed in the UK, Make electrical installation works all notifyable and installed by registered electricians only

Create a new body to review & oversee the Code of Conduct for MPs and sanctions, A new Independent Office of MPs Conduct should be created to review the existing Code of Conduct to ensure it's fit for purpose, on a par with that of other public bodies e.g. the Police, and be given powers to investigate and impose sanctions for alleged breaches of this revised Code of Conduct., These sanctions should include a ban on serving in public office where a serious breach is found. This should help restore public trust in their elected representatives. We believe current processes to enforce the Code of Conduct for MPs are inadequate, and that MPs should have no role in deciding whether the code has been breached, or what sanctions should be applied. 
 
The current systems in place do not have our confidence, and we believe they are ineffective at stopping bad behaviour by our elected MPs, which in turn can have a negative effect on overall governance.
Ban Halal slaughter of animals in the UK, Make the practice Illegal, & enforce the illegality of it., It's cruel and barbaric and regressive.

Install CCTV Cameras on the High Road, Barnet, I would like the Barnet Council to install CCTV cameras in the High Road as there is none, and the residents don't feel safe anymore., Lately, loads of burglaries happened, both cars and houses.
On social media groups of Barnet, I read quite a lot of stories of burglary. This is getting quite constant, we would like some cameras to be installed, as not everyone has a camera in the front of their house.
My car has been stolen in November, by the burglar scanning my car key, then the next day two more happened in my area, and so it went.

QEHB car parking petition, Queen Elizabeth hospital Birmingham car parking charge is now 1% of staffs wages there is never any car parking spaces .why are we paying for parking  when Wales and Scotland NHS staff have parking for free .,

Stop MLA's pay in Northern Ireland until the Executive is formed, Taxpayers face paying out more than £94,000 a week in wages to MLAs and ministers even if the Assembly is not sitting., We want to Government to stop all MLA's Pay in Northern Ireland until the executive is formed.

Use indelible ink to help prevent multiple voting in general elections, I welcome the new legislation to bring about mandatory photographic identification in order to vote in certain elections. This was introduced in 2003 in Northern Ireland under the last Labour government. We need to follow the example of India, the world's largest democracy., In India, they have used fingerprint voting where, on voting, your index finger is marked with indelible ink in order to prevent multiple voting. I welcome photographic ID in order to prove that you have the right to vote but we need to follow the example of the Indian government to prevent multiple fraudulent votes.

Referendum on Brexit from the World Health Organisation, Hold a referendum on the United Kingdom's membership of the World Health Organisation to establish whether it has the confidence of the British people, asking:

"Should the United Kingdom remain a member of the World Health Organisation or leave the World Health Organisation?",

Hold a referendum on the UK's membership of the World Health Organisation, Hold a referendum on the United Kingdom's membership of the World Health Organisation, to establish whether the British public want to remain a member, or leave., The referendum question should be:
 
"Should the United Kingdom remain a member of the World Health Organisation or leave the World Health Organisation?"

Require CCTV in supported living and care homes, To make it a legal requirement for supported living and care homes to have to install cameras in all areas. This should help prevent residents - especially vulnerable disabled people - being mistreated, and ensure there is evidence of any mistreatment, so that action can be taken against offenders.,

Give schoolchildren 5 flexible days off school each year, Introduce 5 flexible days of leave for schoolchildren each year during term time, which children and parents can plan at their convenience. Potentially leveraging tools developed during lockdown such as remote or recorded lessons., School holidays are mostly around the same time creating high demand in the travel industry and resulting in very expensive vacations for families. Though leave can be authorised, practically it’s often denied. The current system also does not reflect professional life for which students should be being prepared, where individuals plan their own leave and ensure their work is not affected.

Have Boris Johnson resign as a result of the Sue Gray report, Boris Johnson, the Prime Minister, has been found to have broken the law, and be in attendance of parties within his place of residence as a result of the Sue Gray report. As such, he should be made to resign as he misled parliament on numerous occasions, Public confidence in Parliament and the Prime Minister are at a low, he has been shown to have broken the rules, or known about rule breaking in his own party, not only this, but he has been fined by the met police for breaking his country's law, which is entirely unacceptable.

Remove the ban on prisoners voting from the Representation of the People Act, The UK’s ban on prisoners voting was ruled to be in breach of the European Convention on Human Rights in 2005. There are a plethora of benefits to be gained from removing this ban: aiding inmates’ rehabilitation; providing a connection to the outside world; and representing their views., Denying voting rights to criminals who receive a custodial sentence is dehumanizing and hinders rehabilitation. It also means politicians do not take the rights, needs and interests of prisoners seriously enough. The Representation of the People Act should be amended to remove this ban and allow all prisoners (not just e.g. those released on temporary licence) to vote. Ultimately, voting is a human right, and it is highly unethical to restrict this for so many.
